learning_need: Project-first practical deep learning for experienced coders
decision_rationale: fast.ai remains one of the strongest pedagogical deep-learning courses reviewed, but its practical stack is centred on recordings and tooling from 2022. In a fast-moving AI category, the canonical set already has substantially more current broad routes through CS50 AI and Google ML Crash Course, so the ageing implementation layer materially reduces present-day marginal value.
marginal_value: Adds excellent project-first deep-learning pedagogy, but not enough current implementation advantage over the existing broad AI and ML incumbents.
provider_concentration_notes: fast.ai has no canonical record; the non-admission is driven by currency and overlap, not provider concentration.
coverage_notes: Deep-learning foundations remain covered by CS50 AI and Google ML Crash Course; fast.ai stays available as a reviewed alternative for learners who value its teaching style.

learning_need: Short current introduction to modern AI concepts and application areas
decision_rationale: Microsoft's path is current and broad, but at under four hours it is primarily conceptual orientation with limited sustained practice. Google ML Crash Course provides a stronger current beginner-to-intermediate technical foundation, while CS50 AI supplies much deeper project work. Currency alone does not justify another introductory AI slot.
marginal_value: Adds a concise vocabulary primer, but insufficient depth and practice to improve the canonical AI foundation set.
provider_concentration_notes: Microsoft has no canonical AI record; this is a direct depth and redundancy decision rather than a provider penalty.
coverage_notes: Modern AI concepts, generative AI and ML fundamentals are already covered by stronger current incumbents.

learning_need: Building AI agents in the Microsoft Azure and Foundry ecosystem
decision_rationale: The Microsoft path is highly current and useful for Azure-specific learners, but the requirement for Microsoft cloud tooling and its ecosystem-specific framing reduce transferability. Hugging Face Agents offers the stronger general multi-framework course with substantial project work and free certification, while the existing OpenAI Academy reference covers a concise current workflow role.
marginal_value: Adds Azure-specific agent implementation, but not enough provider-neutral learning value to justify a third canonical agent route.
provider_concentration_notes: Provider concentration is not the primary issue; vendor lock-in and direct head-to-head competition are decisive.
coverage_notes: General agentic-AI coverage is stronger with the complementary Hugging Face full course and OpenAI workflow reference.

learning_need: Current hands-on multi-framework agentic AI from foundations through evaluation
decision_rationale: Hugging Face Agents materially improves the canonical set because it is a living, structured specialist course rather than a short workflow primer. It progresses through agent foundations, tools, multiple frameworks, agentic RAG, assignments and a benchmarked final challenge, while avoiding mandatory paid cloud infrastructure and providing a fully free certificate route.
marginal_value: Adds a deeper multi-framework agent-building pathway that complements the shorter OpenAI workflow course rather than duplicating it.
provider_concentration_notes: Hugging Face has no canonical AI record, so the admission also improves provider diversity in a fast-moving field.
coverage_notes: Creates a two-level agents path: OpenAI Academy for concise workflow fluency and Hugging Face for deeper implementation, frameworks and evaluation.

learning_need: Specialist machine learning for audio, speech recognition and text-to-speech
decision_rationale: The Audio Course has strong assignments and a useful specialist curriculum, but its 2023 practical stack is materially older in a rapidly changing transformer ecosystem and the learning need is narrow. The core index should not add a specialist audio-ML slot while broader AI foundations remain more transferable and current.
marginal_value: Adds genuine speech and audio specialisation, but with insufficient breadth and currentness for the compact core set.
provider_concentration_notes: Hugging Face is admitted elsewhere for Agents, which raises the marginal bar for an additional specialist course from the same provider.
coverage_notes: Audio ML remains a reviewed specialist option rather than a demonstrated core coverage requirement.

learning_need: Hands-on introductory machine-learning classification workflow in MATLAB
decision_rationale: Machine Learning Onramp is polished and genuinely hands-on, but its narrow classification scope and MATLAB-specific workflow are less transferable than the existing Google and Kaggle foundations. A free certificate and strong browser exercises do not outweigh the duplication and vendor dependence.
marginal_value: Adds low-friction MATLAB practice, but no stronger general ML role than the current canonical beginner and broad interactive routes.
provider_concentration_notes: MathWorks has no canonical AI record; vendor specificity and redundancy drive the decision.
coverage_notes: Beginner machine learning is already strongly covered by Kaggle Intro ML and Google ML Crash Course.

learning_need: Short browser-based deep-learning and transfer-learning practice in MATLAB
decision_rationale: Deep Learning Onramp has excellent immediate practice, but it focuses on a compact MATLAB image-classification workflow. CS50 AI and Google ML Crash Course provide broader, more transferable foundations, and even the non-admitted fast.ai course offers substantially deeper project scope. The specialist vendor workflow does not justify a core slot.
marginal_value: Adds convenient MATLAB transfer-learning practice, but too little breadth and portability for the core index.
provider_concentration_notes: There is no MathWorks concentration issue; the course loses on transferability and scope.
coverage_notes: Deep-learning concepts and applications remain covered by broader canonical AI and ML resources.

learning_need: Short beginner orientation to data science, analytics and data engineering
decision_rationale: Cisco Introduction to Data Science is a legitimate assessed six-hour orientation, but Cisco Data Analytics Essentials is substantially deeper, more practical and portfolio-oriented while remaining beginner-accessible. Admitting both would mirror a provider progression rather than improve the core set.
marginal_value: Adds a gentler orientation, but insufficient distinctiveness beside the much stronger Cisco analytics pathway.
provider_concentration_notes: Provider concentration is directly relevant because the stronger Cisco course serves the broader learner need better.
coverage_notes: Introductory data work remains accessible through Cisco Data Analytics Essentials and the existing beginner ML resources.

learning_need: Broad beginner data analytics with spreadsheets, SQL, visualisation, labs and portfolio work
decision_rationale: Data Analytics Essentials fills a genuine canonical gap outside machine learning. Its roughly 30-hour path integrates spreadsheets, SQL, Tableau, repeated labs, module exams, a final exam and portfolio-oriented analysis. That breadth and assessment structure provide substantially more standalone value than the adjacent Kaggle microcourses or Cisco's shorter introduction.
marginal_value: Adds a complete job-oriented data-analytics foundation rather than another AI or ML course.
provider_concentration_notes: Cisco has no canonical AI/Data record and the course earns admission by covering a distinct learning need with unusually strong practice.
coverage_notes: Closes broad data-analytics coverage while allowing narrower Pandas, visualisation and SQL microcourses to remain supplements rather than separate core entries.

learning_need: Fast hands-on Pandas onboarding for Python data manipulation
decision_rationale: Kaggle Pandas is an excellent four-hour skills module with immediate notebook practice, but it is not a standalone data-analysis foundation. With Kaggle Intro ML already canonical and Cisco Data Analytics Essentials admitted for broader analyst skills, another adjacent Kaggle microcourse would add catalogue concentration faster than learning coverage.
marginal_value: Adds focused Pandas fluency, but not enough breadth or distinctiveness for a separate core slot.
provider_concentration_notes: Kaggle already has a canonical Intro ML course, so adjacent microcourses face a higher marginal-value threshold.
coverage_notes: Pandas remains a useful reviewed supplement; broad data-analysis needs are covered by Cisco Data Analytics Essentials.

learning_need: Short hands-on Python data visualisation using Seaborn
decision_rationale: The course has strong practice density and a final project, but four hours of Seaborn-focused visualisation is too narrow for a core slot and carries library-version currency risk. Cisco Data Analytics Essentials covers visualisation inside a broader analyst pathway, while Kaggle is already represented canonically.
marginal_value: Adds focused plotting practice, but insufficient durable breadth to improve the compact canonical set.
provider_concentration_notes: Existing Kaggle representation makes another adjacent microcourse difficult to justify without a unique high-priority role.
coverage_notes: Data visualisation remains covered inside the admitted Cisco analytics foundation; the Kaggle course stays a useful specialist supplement.

learning_need: Low-friction introductory SQL practice in hosted BigQuery
decision_rationale: Kaggle Intro to SQL is accessible and practical, but CS50 SQL is a substantially stronger canonical database course covering querying, schema design, indexing, optimisation and scaling. Cisco Data Analytics Essentials also provides SQL in a broader analyst context. A three-hour BigQuery microcourse does not add enough marginal value.
marginal_value: Adds very low setup friction, but not stronger or broader SQL learning than the existing database incumbent.
provider_concentration_notes: Kaggle is already represented in the canonical AI set, reinforcing the redundancy decision.
coverage_notes: SQL coverage is already excellent through CS50 SQL, with Cisco analytics adding job-oriented contextual practice.

learning_need: Compact follow-on SQL practice with joins, window functions and BigQuery nested data
decision_rationale: Advanced SQL adds useful window-function and nested-data practice, but it remains a four-hour BigQuery-oriented follow-on rather than a complete advanced database course. CS50 SQL is the stronger transferable incumbent, and admitting both Kaggle SQL microcourses would create unnecessary provider and topic duplication.
marginal_value: Adds targeted BigQuery techniques, but not enough general database depth for a core slot.
provider_concentration_notes: Kaggle concentration is material because the platform already has a canonical ML course and multiple reviewed adjacent microcourses.
coverage_notes: Advanced relational database learning remains better served by CS50 SQL; BigQuery-specific skills can stay supplemental.

learning_need: Accessible Portuguese-language overview of artificial intelligence and machine learning
decision_rationale: The NAU route has real pt-PT accessibility and a free credential, but its approximately eight-hour breadth produces limited technical depth and practice across too many AI topics. Language diversity is valuable, yet Phase 4 should not lower the core quality bar when a stronger current ML route already offers Portuguese-language support through Google.
marginal_value: Adds pt-PT delivery and a certificate, but insufficient technical depth to improve the core learning set.
provider_concentration_notes: Provider concentration is not a concern; the decision is based on depth and marginal instructional value.
coverage_notes: Portuguese accessibility remains partly supported by Google ML Crash Course in pt-BR; a stronger pt-PT technical course would still be a legitimate future gap.

learning_need: Very short Portuguese-language introduction to AI concepts, ethics and applications
decision_rationale: At roughly three hours, this course is useful AI literacy but cannot provide enough depth or practice for a top-tier core index. The longer NAU AI/ML course is itself not strong enough to enter, while Google ML Crash Course offers a substantially deeper and more current practical foundation.
marginal_value: Adds accessible pt-PT literacy, but too little instructional depth for a separate canonical entry.
provider_concentration_notes: Provider concentration is irrelevant; the course fails the core depth threshold on its own merits.
coverage_notes: The course remains a reviewed literacy option, but the index should wait for a stronger pt-PT technical AI pathway rather than fill the gap artificially.
